newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London slid across the board with the spot November contract touching nearby support at $1,515 a tonne. The drawdown in green coffee stocks in the United States was apparently not enough to hold prices up. November closed $12 weaker at $1,516 while January shed $26 to close at $1,433.

In New York for the first time this month the December/March spread did not widen. Initially the market jumped in response to the Green Coffee Association data released yesterday which showed a further erosion in US stock levels to 1.6 million bags, but then strong origin sales turned the market around and a combination of producer selling and local pressure sent the market lower.

The slide was seen as a correction to recent gains and prices are expected to remain firm. December lost 2.00 cents/lb to close at 112.20 cents/lb while March gave up 1.65 cents/lb to end at 103.55 cents/lb. The outer months finished 1.25 to 1.70 cents/lb lower.
ACPC - The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said it will cease to publish its coffee retention indicator prices, without giving any further explanation.

BRAZIL - Brazil's green coffee exporters expect October shipments to weigh-in at 1.7-1.8 million 60-kg bags, a spokesman for the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (FEBEC) said. Brazil's green coffee exports fell to 1.14 million bags in September, from 1.54 million bags in August.
This was attributed to the fact that many exporters had held back their shipments until Congress passed a law removing a 13 per cent sales tax from coffee exports.

Under the ACPC retention plan Brazil can ship 9 million bags in the six months between July and December 1996. In the first three months it shipped only 3.85 million bags which means that it could still ship around 1.7 million bags in each of the next three months and still be in line with the ACPC limit.

In the following six months (January/June 1997), Brazilian exports should not exceed 6 million bags but already exporters have expressed concern about availability given crop size and strong internal demand.

One additional source of supply is government stocks. A series of monthly auctions is planned but so far only small quantities have been sold due to the domestic harvest. On October 23 it is planned to auction 69,783 60-kg bags. However, the auctions are likely to increase in size from the beginning of 1997 but will probably continue below the current limit of 200,000 bags per month, it was said.

PORTUGAL - Portugal imported 56,433 bags of coffee in June 1996, 2.8 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 371,500 bags, 23 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell by 5.6 per cent to 626,500 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Cameroon (30,300 vs 21,300 bags), Ivory Coast (52,300 vs 37,400 bags) and Brazil (49,800 vs 42,500 bags).
The country exported 47,300 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 39 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose by 41 per cent to 73,500 bags.
